defect_2_sub_case_fixture_lifetime.why_failures_still_surface: doCleanups records a failing cleanup against the enclosing sub-case rather than swallowing it, and ExitStack re-raises out of the `with`, where subTest records it. A broken teardown is still a reported outcome.

what_this_run_did_NOT_establish: WHY run 345388 saw sqlite3 'database or disk is full' and this run did not. The outcome did not reproduce here, in isolation or in the full gate, at the base or under the candidate as given. The strongest supported explanation -- and it is not proven -- is that /tmp is a 64 MiB tmpfs SHARED with the provider's own ephemera, that run 345388 worked for 789 seconds before its gate ran, and that the gate's then-13.3 MB peak met a /tmp that the turn had already largely consumed. This run observed 56-57 MB available at gate time; what 345388 had available at its gate time was never recorded and cannot now be recovered. THIS IS THE ONE OPERAND FINDING: /tmp is 67108864 bytes total, it is not the gate's alone, and nothing bounds what else consumes it. Reported with numbers and NOT acted on -- no limit was changed and no TMPDIR was moved.
